21.    When enquired about the details of encouraging private sector participation and framing of guidelines for involvement of private sector for development of infrastructure services in
 the port sector, the Department of Shipping informed that the existing policy dispensation provides for private sector participation including foreign direct investment upto 100% in the
 port sector. The Government's endeavour is to provide a facilitative investor friendly environment with transparent procedures and decision making process for encouraging private sector
 participation in the sector.  The Government has, issued comprehensive guidelines for attracting private sector participation in major ports as also for formation of joint ventures by major
 ports for development of infrastructure services. The guidelines preferred route for private sector participation through open competitive bidding in which the bidder offering the highest
 percentage of revenue share out of the operation of the facility is selected.  Tariff Authority for Major ports (TAMP) which is an independent statutory authority fixes the tariffs to be
 charged from the port users by the private operators. These tariffs act as a ceiling and the private operators are free to charge below these ceilings.
 
22.    The major ports can also form joint ventures with publicly owned foreign ports for attracting new technology, introducing better managerial practices, etc.  In case it is considered
 that certain technology, expertise, managerial practices are necessary to be imported from a particular country, Government to Government arrangements for formation of a joint venture
 between a major port in India and a foreign port to be selected by the foreign Government can also be considered.  These joint ventures can be formed without following the tender route. 
 The form of collaboration will be on BOT basis.

 Five Year Plan period will continue to be on the following:-
(i)                  Enhancing productivity of Major Ports through technology up gradation.
(ii)                Cost effective service.
(iii)               Improving service-quality
(iv)              Efficient management, institutional funding and attracting private investments.

TONNAGE TAX
 
28.       The Government has announced introduction of Tonnage Tax from the financial year 2004-05 for the Shipping Industry with an option for the shipping companies to opt for either
 tonnage tax or corporate tax. This will facilitate investment in shipping sector. The silent features
of the tonnage tax regime are:-
Ø      The introduction of Tonnage tax will provide a level playing field to the Indian Shipping    Industry with its international counterparts.
 
Ø      This will be implemented from the current financial year. 
Ø      At least 20% of the book profits of the companies opting for tonnage tax scheme to be    transferred to a separate reserve to be utilized for acquisition of vessels within 8 years. This
 will help to add more tonnage to the Indian Shipping industry.
 
Ø      Provision regarding mandatory minimum training requirements for the companies opting for the proposed Tonnage Tax regime. 
 
Ø      The shipping companies are to opt either of Tonnage Tax or Corporation tax.
 
Ø      An option for tonnage tax has to be exercised by the company once. The Tonnage Tax regime would remain applicable for 10 years, for the companies opting for the same. 
 
29.       Dredgers have also been included in the Tonnage Tax regime from 2005-06. The Government has been making constant efforts for creating hospitable investment environment for
 the Shipping Industry.  Some of the efforts made/steps taken are as under:
Ø                              Prior to introduction of Tonnage tax, the Indian Shipping Industry were enjoying the benefits under Section 33AC of IT Act. Under Section 33AC shipping
 companies were allowed to create reserves upto twice the paid up capital and reserves including share premium account, which they were supposed to be utilized in next 8 years
 for acquisition of vessels. The amounts so transferred in the reserve were exempted from corporate tax;
 
Ø
                              Import of all types of ships has been included in the Open General Licence (OGL) thereby dispensing with licence requirement for import of various kind of
 ships, as per guidelines issued by the Ministry of Shipping on 15th June,2001 and 5th March,2002 ;
 
Ø                              100 percent Foreign Direct Investment  (FDI) is allowed in Shipping sector;
30.       Regarding extending the benefit of tonnage tax to the vessels registered under Indian Vessels Act, 1917 and Indian Coasting Vessels Act, 1838, the Department of Shipping in its
 written reply stated that while presenting the Finance bill for 2005-06, the Finance Minister has pronounced extension of tonnage tax regime for dredgers only.  However, for vessels
 registered under Indian Vessels Act 1917 and Indian Coastal Vessels Act, 1838 the benefit of tonnage tax has not been extended in this bill.  The issue is being taken up with Ministry of
 Finance for extending the benefits to these types of vessels also.
           
31.       The Committee notes that the Government has since introduced the tonnage tax regime to the dredgers also as per its recommendation.  The Committee feels that introduction of
 tonnage tax in lieu of corporate tax will not only facilitate investment in shipping sector but also provide a level playing field to the Indian Shipping Industry vis-à-vis its foreign
 counterparts and the shipping companies will be able to acquire more tonnage.  However, the Committee is unable to comprehend the reasons for excluding the vessels registered under
 the Indian Vessels Act 1917 and Indian coastal vessel Act, 1838.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the matter for extending the benefits of tonnage tax to the vessels registered
 under Indian Vessels Act 1917 and Indian Coastal Vessels Act, 1838 may be pursued further with the Ministry of Finance as this also vitally linked to the viability of the Inland Water
 Transport sector.
 
SETHUSAMUDRAM SHIP CHANNEL PROJECT
32.       India does not have a continuous navigable route around the peninsula within her own territorial waters due to presence of a reef called Adam's Bridge at Pamban near
 Rameshwaram.  Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project envisages cutting of a ship channel to connect the Gulf of Mannar to Bay of Bengal through Palk Bay so that most of the ships,
 depending on the draft required, moving between east and west coast of India could have a continuous navigable sea route around the Peninsula within India's own territorial waters.  This
 will save upto 424 nautical miles of travel and upto about 30 hours of sailing time for ships between east and west coast.    The project will serve the strategic and national security
 interests of the country since the channel can also be used by Naval and Coast Guard ships.  The project is also expected to spur overall economic development of coastal districts of
 Tamilnadu through development of infrastructure, ancillary industries etc. 
33.       To a specific query regarding adverse environmental effects of the proposed channel, the Department of Shipping in its written reply stated that a section of environmentalists have
 expressed their concerns about the potential adverse effects of the proposed channel on environment.  The main apprehensions expressed are:
(a)                Environmental Impact such as effect on marine flora and fauna, oil spillage, increased salinity in waterbed etc.
(b)               Economic Impact such as loss of livelihood of fishermen due to reduction in fish catches.

CRUISE SHIPPING
37.       Cruise shipping is a fast growing sector globally. As a departure from concept of cargo and passenger ships, cruise is like a moving township studded with all state of art facilities
 including all types of recreational activities. The idea is fast catching, because, journey on a cruise is not only pleasurable, but also almost free from sea travel health hazards. Experience
 gained in the Caribbean, Latin American and South-East Asian countries indicates that huge amount of foreign exchange can be earned by providing the right policy environment and
 infrastructure for the growth of cruise shipping. India with its vast and beautiful coastline, virgin forests and undisturbed idyllic islands, long historical and cultural tradition of
 architecture, theatre and performing arts can prove to be fabulous destination for cruise-tourists.  The global scenario for cruise shipping is picking up very fast, with an annual increment
 from 10-20% in the cruise ship fleet and passengers carried. Further, Indian coastline is unfortunately not witnessing the same growth pattern as mentioned.  Therefore, it is said that a
 strong policy intervention by the Government of India would be necessary for its stimulated growth. 
 
38.       To a specific question regarding efforts for growth of cruise shipping in India, the Department of Shipping in its written reply submitted that in order to formulate cruise shipping
 policy a High Power Steering Group under the Chairmanship of Minister of Shipping, Road Transport & Highways and Union Minister of State for Tourism (Independent Charge) as Co-
Chairperson has been set up on 29.9.2004.  The first meeting of this Group was held on 14
th December 2004 in which the draft Concept and Policy Paper for Cruise Shipping in India was
 discussed at length.  Various issues concerning this sector have been taken up and Working Groups have been formed to tackle all the issues.  Three Working Groups have already
 finalized their reports, which will come up before the Steering Group for providing finality to their recommendations.  Other Groups are also progressing well and it is hoped that very
 soon their recommendations will be compiled and given a final shape to the proposed policy.  The draft policy paper has also been deliberated by the Consultative Committee of this
 Ministry in its Meeting held on 20.12.2004.  A Workshop was also convened at Mumbai on 12.2.2005 which was attended by Members of the Consultative Committee, various
 stakeholders, hospitality industry, shipping lines, cruise lines, tour operators and shipping agents.  Once a policy is in place, besides providing a direction to the growth of cruise shipping,
 it will also remove the bottlenecks pertaining to the sector.
39.       The Committee desired to know the details of private sector participation for development of infrastructure and other facilities at various ports, the Department of Shipping in its
 written reply informed that working group comprising of the representatives of Department of Tourism, the major ports and the industry was constituted by Department of Shipping for
 identification of ports for development of cruise facilities.  The Group has recommended that in the first phase, 6 major ports of call by the cruise liners namely, Mumbai, Mormugao, New
 Mangalore, Cochin, Tuticorin and Chennai be selected for the development of infrastructure and other facilities so as to make India as an attractive cruise destination.  In the second phase,
 the major port of Kolkata and minor ports at Puri, Porbandar and Port Blair have been recommended for development of cruise facilities.  Further, if any major/minor port is able to attract
 a BOT operator to invest in infrastructure facilities, the port may develop such facility. The development of cruise tourism infrastructure is to be done through port resources, financial
 support from Ministry of Tourism under their scheme for promoting tourism as well as private sector investment.  Private sector participation will be encouraged for the development of
 cruise tourism infrastructure, wherever viable. 
 
40.       The Committee is of the view that sea travel is becoming increasingly popular and there is enormous potential for its growth and expansion in India.  The Committee notes that six
 major ports- Mumbai, Mormugao, New Mangalore, Kochi, Tuticorin and Chennai have been identified for the development of infrastructure and other facilities with a view to make India
 an attractive cruise destination.  The Committee notes that a High Power Steering Group has been set up with a view to catalyze the growth and development of cruise shipping and to
 remove bottlenecks and a policy is being formulated in the regard. The Committee hopes that the group will submit its report expeditiously and the policy is framed at the earliest so that

42.       The Committee enquired about the status of the proposal sent  to Ministry of Finance for release of grants in aids to Calcutta Dock Labour Board, the Department of Shipping
 informed that the proposal for release of enhanced grant of Rs.59.59 crores to Calcutta Dock Labour Board to meet its pensionary liabilities on account of revision of pensionary benefits
 as per wage settlement and for liberalization of post retirement benefits to pensioners who retired before 1.1.1998 was taken up with Ministry of Finance who has not accepted the
 proposal on account of the following :-
(i)            Section 124 of the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 makes it abundantly clear that no regulation made by the port shall take effect unless it is approved by the Central Government
 and until such approval has been published in the Official Gazette.  Since the rules and regulations concerning pension have not been approved by Department of Expenditure,
 these regulations do not appear to have any legal sanctity;
(ii)           Department of Expenditure as a matter of policy do not agree to the proposal for introduction of pension scheme on Government of India pattern in the autonomous bodies;
(iii)          The Act governing service conditions of employees of Port Trusts/Dock Labour Boards also stipulate that the Port Trusts/Dock Labour Boards will generate their own resources
 to meet the financial liability on account of payment of salaries/pension, etc.  In this regard, the present pension fund size of the major Port Trusts is sufficient to provide for only
 20% of the pension out-go in case pensionary benefits at par with Central Government are allowed for the employees who had joined these bodies till 31.12.2003.  It has been
 opined that the resources available with these bodies do not justify extension of pension scheme on Government of India pattern. Further, permission in one case will lead to
 similar demand from employees of other autonomous bodies.
(iv)          Permission if any, accorded from Department of Expenditure at this stage will negate the very purpose with which New Pension Scheme based on defined contributions has been
 introduced w.e.f. 1.1.2004.  The New Pension Scheme has already been extended to the employees of autonomous institutions/PSUs.

MISAPPROPRIATION OF SEAMEN'S PROVIDENT FUND
52.       The Seamen’s Provident Fund Scheme as a social security scheme for Indian Merchant Navy Seamen's was brought under statute by enactment of the Seamen's Provident Fund
 Act, 1966 and introduced retrospectively with effect from 1
st July 1964 to provide for the institution of a provident fund for seamen as old age retirement benefit and for their family
 members in the event of death of seamen members.  This was a contributory Provident Fund and the employees were required to deposit the Provident Fund contributions in respect of
 Seamen employed by them with their watching contribution with Seamen's Provident Fund Organisation after the terminations of each voyage.  The prevailing rate of contribution was 12
 percent of the wages.  All money belonging to the Funds were invested in the Securities as per the pattern prescribed by the Ministry of Finance. The position of investment is as under:-

INDIAN INSTITUTE OF MARITIME STUDIES(IIMS)
57.       In order to make appropriate changes in the institutional frame work and financial arrangements for imparting maritime training with the active participation of the Industry and
 keeping in view the need to augment maritime training facilities, including the feasibility and desirability of bringing the institutes under a university type of structure, the Government of
 India in October 1991 set up a committee on Maritime Education & Training (COMET).  The committee in its report submitted in May 1992, recommended establishment of an autonomous
 apex body named as Indian Maritime University to manage, control, supervise, direct and monitor the Maritime Training Institutions functioning under the Government control.  
 Accordingly Indian Institute of Maritime Studies (IIMS) was registered as a Society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 on 6 th June 2002 and as a Charitable Trust under Bombay
 Public Trusts Act, 1950 on 15 th January 2003.  The four Maritime Training Institutions, namely (1) Lal Bahadur Sashtri College of Advanced Maritime Studies and Research, Mumbai, (2)
 T.S. Chanakya, Navi Mumbai, (3) Marine Engineering and Research Institute, Kolkata and (4) Marine Engineering and Research Institute, Mumbai have been placed within the domain of
 Indian Institute of Maritime Studies.
 
58.       As regards, establishment of Indian Maritime  University under an Act of Parliament, the Department of Shipping in its written reply informed the Committee that an Expert
 Committee including representatives of University Grants Commission has been constituted to look into the feasibility of formation of Indian Maritime  University (IMU). The
 Committee held several meetings and visited training institutes at Mumbai and Kolkata and recommended for the formation of Indian Maritime University by an Act of Parliament
 under the aegis of Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways, Department of Shipping. As a consequence to this a draft Indian Maritime University Bill has been prepared.
 
59.       To the specific querry regarding fixing time limit for the establishment of Indian Maritime University, the Department of Shipping stated that the financial implications are
 being worked out. It is expected that the Indian Maritime University may probably come into existence during 2005-06. Keeping this in view, a token provision of Rs.1.00 crore on the
 Plan side has been made during the financial year 2005-06 for development of Indian Maritime University.

 Committee on Accommodation has been sent to Cabinet Secretariat on 7.2.2005 for consideration. As regards, creation of pension fund and finalization of terms and conditions for the
 absorption of employees of Indian Institute of Marine Studies, it is stated that till the employees are on deemed deputation to Indian Institute of Maritime Studies and absorbed therein,
 they continue to be Government servants. Thus, creation of pension fund and settling of terms and conditions appears to be premature at this stage. Moreover, in the wake of

INLAND WATER TRANSPORT
 92.      Inland Water Transport (IWT) is an efficient mode of transport from the point of view of energy consumption, cost of transportation of environment friendliness. IWAI executes
 various Schemes for development of the Inland Water Transport infrastructure namely fairway development, terminals, and navigational aids for National Waterways.  So far, following
 three waterways have been declared as national waterways:-
National Waterway No.1 (NW-1)
            Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system from Allahabad to Haldia (1620 kms) - declared as national waterway in 1986.
National Waterway No.2 (NW-2)
            The Brahmaputra river from Sadiya to Dhubri (891 kms) - declared as national waterway in 1988.
National Waterway No.3 (NW-3)
            The west coast canal from Kollam to Kottapuram alongwith Champakara and Udyogmandal canais (205 kms) - declared as national waterway in 1993.

(iii)       East Coast Canal along with river Brahmani and Mahanadi delta

OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS
AT A GLANCE
 
ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2005-06
            The Committee expresses its concern over the failure of Department of Shipping to spend the approved outlay.  During the year 2004-05, out of the budgeted amount of Rs.2419.66
 crore the Department could spent only Rs.1400.99 crore which clearly indicates the poor fiscal management in the Department of Shipping.  The Committee observes that even while
 revising allocations, little consideration has been paid to the actual expenditure incurred in the past.  This shows that budgetary and revised estimates have always been made without
 taking into account the actual requirements as experienced in the previous years.
           
The Committee feels that Department of Shipping has not evolved effective system or planning to systematically anticipate, assess and project its actual requirements of funds
 otherwise the investments could have yielded commensurate returns.  The Committee recommends that in future, the Department of Shipping should be transparent and realistic while
 making projections of required funds so that resources may not remain unused and are allocated more judiciously.

REPORT
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/86threport.htm[28-08-2018 13:09:34]
(Paras 10 & 11)
PORT SECTOR
The Committee is unhappy with the poor performance of Department of Shipping with regard to under utilization of approved outlays over the years for the port sector.  During the
 Financial year 2004-05, an outlay of Rs.1066.55 crore was allocated for the port sector but the ports could utilize only Rs.440.51 crore. The Committee is dismayed by this repeated failure
 of Department of Shipping and is surprised as to why the Ministry asks for so much of allocation if it is not in position to spend the approved outlay. The Committee desires that the
 Department of Shipping should take all corrective measures based upon actual requirements for maximum utilization of budgeted amount during 2005-06.  In this regard, the Committee
 reiterates its earlier recommendation contained in 81st report of Demands for Grants (2004-05) of Ministry of Shipping which reads as under:-
"The Committee fails to understand as to how the physical targets will be achieved with this low utilization pattern.  In fact, the Committee feels that this raises doubts about
 the mismatch in the projections for physical and financial targets.  The Committee is of the view that the Ministry of Shipping has full responsibility to ensure proper
 utilization of the approved outlay.  The Committee feels that strict monitoring is crucial for timely completion of any project.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that
 the monitoring agency should play rather proactive role and do away with the procedural hurdles for timely completion of the projects so that the budgeted allocation is
 utilized optimally.  The Committee also recommends the Ministry to keep informed about the progress in the matter."
            (Para 16)
CAPACITY AND TRAFFIC IN MAJOR PORT
            The Committee expresses its appreciation for achievement of the capacity of major ports which has either exceeded the target or likely to achieve target fixed for cargo handling of
 all commodities except container.  The containerization is the emerging global trend in the mode of cargo trade in which the country is lagging behind which is a matter of concern.
           
The Committee feels that a proper environment with transparent procedures and decision making process can give boost to private sector participation in the port sector.  The
 Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to review the existing guidelines on Private Sector Participation in the port sector with emphasis on overcoming capital
 constraints, technology upgradation and value addition.
(Paras 26 & 27)
TONNAGE TAX
            The Committee notes that the Government has since introduced the tonnage tax regime to the dredgers also as per its recommendation.  The Committee feels that introduction of
 tonnage tax in lieu of corporate tax will not only facilitate investment in shipping sector but also provide a level playing field to the Indian Shipping Industry vis-à-vis its foreign
 counterparts and the shipping companies will be able to acquire more tonnage.  However, the Committee is unable to comprehend the reasons for excluding the vessels registered under
 the Indian Vessels Act 1917 and Indian coastal vessel Act, 1838.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the matter for extending the benefits of tonnage tax to the vessels registered
 under Indian Vessels Act 1917 and Indian Coastal Vessels Act, 1838 may be pursued further with the Ministry of Finance as this also vitally linked to the viability of the Inland Water
 Transport sector.
(Para 31)
SETHUSAMUDRAM SHIP CHANNEL PROJECT
            The Committee notes the Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project is of great economic and strategic importance which will connect the Gulf of Mannar to Bay of Bengal so that the
 ship moving between East and West coast of India could have a continuous navigable sea route within their own territorial waters and the proposed channel save upto 424 nautical miles of
 travel and about 30 hours of sailing time for ships.  The Committee notes with satisfaction that Ministry of Environment & Forests has also given environmental clearance to the project
 and a special purpose vehicle has been incorporated to raise finance to create and operate navigable channel.  The Committee expects that the project once completed will serve the
 strategic and national security interests besides spuring the overall economic development of coastal districts of southern states.  The Committee however, recommends that while taking
 up the implementation of the project, the Department of Shipping must give due attention to the likely effect of natural calamities particularly one like as Tsunami which hit southern
 states during December 2004 and safety measures may be incorporated accordingly.
  (Para 36)
CRUISE SHIPPING
            The Committee is of the view that sea travel is becoming increasingly popular and there is enormous potential for its growth and expansion in India.  The Committee notes that six
 major ports- Mumbai, Mormugao, New Mangalore, Kochi, Tuticorin and Chennai have been identified for the development of infrastructure and other facilities with a view to make India
 an attractive cruise destination.  The Committee notes that a High Power Steering Group has been set up with a view to catalyze the growth and development of cruise shipping and to
 remove bottlenecks and a policy is being formulated in the regard. The Committee hopes that the group will submit its report expeditiously and the policy is framed at the earliest so that
 the benefit of opportunity available to cruise tourism sector is exploited.  The Committee recommends that pending finalization of policy, the Department of Shipping must take steps to
 attract investments from private sector with a view to create infrastructure and other facilities for development of cruise shipping especially in ports on the Eastern parts of the country
 including Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshdweep Islands having great potential in that area.
(Para 40)
CALCUTTA  DOCK LABOUR BOARD
            The Committee is distressed to note that the employees of the Calcutta Dock Labour Board are not being treated as Government employees so far as payment of pension and
 pensionary benefits are concerned, though, the Calcutta Dock Labour Board, a body corporate, was constituted in terms of section 5(A) of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment)
 Act, 1948 in September 1952.  The Committee expresses its concern that inspite of specific provisions under the Act, the rules and regulations concerning pension for employees of
 Calcutta Dock Labour Board have not been approved by Department of Expenditure and the employees of Calcutta Dock Labour Board are being made victims under the cover that
 Calcutta Dock Labour Board constitutes an autonomous body and therefore, denied of the benefits for long.

REPORT
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/86threport.htm[28-08-2018 13:09:34]
 
            The Committee is of the firm opinion that liabilities on account of payment of arrears of pensions and pensionary dues of Calcutta Dock Labour Board entirely lies on the
 Government and the Government cannot be absolved of its liability and withhold pension and post retirement benefits to the employees of Calcutta Dock Labour Board on one pretext or
 other.  The Committee, strongly recommends, the Department of Shipping to vigorously pursue the matter with Ministry of Finance for release of enhanced grant to Calcutta Dock Labour
 Board for meeting its pensionary liabilities and implement comprehensive restructuring of Calcutta Dock Labour Board for introduction of Voluntary Retirement Scheme.
 
            The Committee is of the view that problem for payment of pension and pensionary dues can be resolved once and for all, if the Government approves self-sustaining proposal for
 Calcutta Dock Labour Board's pensioners with provisions for an initial corpus and an appropriate policy and methodology for payment of pension worked out for the future.  The
 Committee, therefore reiterates, that the Government should build a corpus of pension fund for discharging the future pensionary liabilities of the Board, as the bulk of its employees will
 retire in another two years.
(Paras 49, 50 &51)
MISAPPROPRIATION OF SEAMEN'S PROVIDENT FUND
            The Committee is deeply concerned that the shortage to the tune of Rs.92.78 crore in Seamen's Provident Fund, which lost due to security scam, has not yet been recouped by the
 Department of Shipping.  The Committee is unable to comprehend the reasons for delay in recouping the fund, which is entirely managed by the Government and feels that any further
 delay may cause adverse impact in protection of interests of the seamen's whose life long savings stands jeopardized in the scam.  The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department
 of Shipping to approach the Ministry of Finance for grants-in-aid to recoup the shortage in the Seamen's Provident Fund.
 
            The Committee further recommends that in order to ensure that such happenings are not repeated in future, sufficient legislative and administrative safeguards have to be built in the
 system.  At the same time, those responsible for such scam should not be spared and suitable action including criminal action ought to be taken against them so that such actions provide
 deterrence to other as well.  The Committee would like to be apprised of the action in this regard.
(Paras 55 & 56)
INDIAN INSTITUTE OF MARITIME STUDIES (IIMS)
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Department of Shipping is in the process of drafting Indian Maritime University Bill for the establishment of Indian Maritime
 University under an Act of Parliament and a token provision has been made by the Government for development of Indian Maritime  University. The Committee feels that the move will
 certainly give boost to quality education in the field of marine training.  However, the Committee is unhappy to note that no definite time limit has been fixed for establishment of Indian
 Maritime University and recommends, the Department of Shipping to fix definite time frame for the establishment of Indian Maritime University under a Central Act.  The Committee
 further hopes that while finalizing the location of the Indian Maritime University, existing infrastructure and assests have to be taken into cognizance. 
           
The Committee hopes that the issues pertaining to creation of pension fund and finalization of terms & condition for the absorption of employees of Indian Institute of Maritime
 Studies will be taken care of by the Department without any disadvantage to the employees in the draft bill itself and recommends the Department of Shipping to apprise the Committee of
 the development in this regard.
(Paras 62 & 63)
HINDUSTAN SHIPYARD LIMITED
            The Committee takes note of the fact that Hindustan Shipyard Limited is changing its marketing strategy by engaging itself in the utilization of installed capacity for increasing
 ship-repair turnover.  The vigorous marketing efforts are showing results  and Hindustan Shipyard Limited has been able to secure the hi-tech, hi-value repair orders for betterment of the
 financial health of the yard.  The Committee appreciates the decision of the Government for rehabilitation of Hindustan Shipyard Limited by way of financial restructuring for improving
 the performance of the yard and recommends for expeditious clearance of the proposal for the capital restructuring of the Hindustan Shipyard Limited.                                     
(Para 76)
HOOGHLY DOCK & PORT ENGINEERS LIMITED
            The Committee is happy to note that a rehabilitation-cum-revival package has been prepared for Hooghly Dock & Port Engineers Limited and a token provision has also been kept
 for the purpose as per its recommendation.  The Committee is of the opinion that Hooghly Dock & Port Engineers Limited with its infrastructure and a expertise can be a integral part for
 development and promotion of Inland Water Transport through NW-1 and NW-2 and contribute to the national economy as well. The Committee, therefore recommends the Government
 to grant clearance for the revival package of Hooghly Dock & Port Engineers Limited expeditiously.
(Para 82)
CENTRAL INLAND WATER TRANSPORT CORPORATION
The Committee notes with distress that the matter for disinvestments of Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd has been referred to the Board for Reconstruction of Public
 Sector Enterprises.  The Committee feels that the Government has not made much efforts to improve the financial health of the company.  The Committee is gravely concern by the fact
 that inspite of repeated recommendation in the past the Government has not yet been able to come out with a complete blueprint for making full use of the existing assets of the company
 in ensuring productive potential by exploring all possibilities like merger with similar entities and integration with Inland Water Transport. The Committee is firmly of the view that the
 future of Inland Water Transport operations including that of Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd holds immense possibilities for establishing a well-defined multimodal
 transportation network in the country and therefore recommends the Department of Shipping to take steps to improve the performance of the Central Inland Water Transport Corporation
 Ltd besides impressing upon the Ministry of Finance for capital restructuring with its existing infrastructure, capacity and manpower.
(Para 91)
INLAND WATER TRANSPORT

REPORT
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/86threport.htm[28-08-2018 13:09:34]
            The Committee is constrained to note that Inland Water Transport has been the most neglected sector and has not been developed with desired pace inspite of its economic potential
 and merely accounts for 0.15% of cargo movement in the country.  The Committee observes that though measures to boost the growth of cargo traffic have been put in place and
 department is committed to raise the share of Inland Water Transport to 2% over the next 8-20 years. The Committee however, notes that with a view to compete with the other developed
 modes of transport, the Department of Shipping is working on declaration and development of three more waterways as National Waterways and a task force to monitor the progress of
 Inland Water Transport projects has also been formed. The Committee, recommends the Department of Shipping to exploit the full potential of this efficient mode of transport, besides,
 addressing the issues of development of adequate infrastructure facilities namely fairways, terminal and navigational aids on the existing three NWs.
 
            The Committee also recommends the Government to improve the modal-mix of transport in the country and prepare a road map for integrated transport policy to include   Inland
 Water Transport, Coastal Shipping, Civil Aviation, Road Transport & Highways and Railways.
            The Committee is perturbed to note the practice of under utilization of budgeted amount by the Department of Shipping over the years.  During 2004-05, the Department of
 Shipping has projected Rs.133.50 crore plan outlays for Inland Water Transport sector, which was reduced to Rs.121.03 at R.E. stage, and ultimately the Department of Shipping has spent
 only Rs.80.00 crore during 2004-05.  The Committee observes that actual expenditure incurred has always been low compared to the budget estimates for Inland Water Transport sector
 including North-East Pool of fund.  The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to intensify its monitoring mechanism to ensure that the budgeted amounts
 earmarked at the B.E. stage are fully utilized during 2005-06.  At the same time the Committee desires that the Department of Shipping should review all the on-going schemes and if
 required, re-allocate the funds budgeted during the financial year.
 
            The Committee notes that a comprehensive Inland Water Transport policy has been announced by the Government to encourage investment from the Private-Public participation
 for accelerated development of Inland Water Transport sector.  The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Department of Shipping for creating transparent, hospitable and conducive
 environment for ensuring both the Private and Public sector participation in the development of Inland Water Transport sector.  The Committee expects that primarily public investment in
 Inland Water Transport sector will definitely help to create infrastructure facilities and augment Inland Water Transport fleet.  The Committee recommends that all pending Inland Water
 Transport specific projects should be cleared expeditiously.
           
The Committee notes with dismay that Research & Development Studies facilities especially in design of vessels and night navigation facilities and identification of economically
 viable routes for development of Inland Water Transport sector has not been given due consideration.  The Committee is of the view that Research & Development activities is the
 backbone for success of any sector and recommends the Department of Shipping to strengthen the Research & Development facilities for development of Inland Water Transport Sector in
 the country.
           
The Committee is happy to note that Department of Shipping has appointed a consultant for working out a realistic target for cargo transportation vis-à-vis targeted investments for
 Inland Water Transport promotion for the 10
th Plan and beyond as per its recommendation.  The Committee hopes that the study for linking the investment in Inland Water Transport
 sector with achievement of physical targets for cargo transportation will certainly enhance the prospects of Inland Water Transport and help to boost the growth of cargo traffic in Inland
 Water Transport sector. The Committee directs the Department of Shipping to apprise it about the progress in the matter.
(Paras 98, 99, 104, 106, 108 & 110)

coordination of activities of various Central Government agencies, State Governments/Union Territories and the Private Sector for the
development and promotion of tourism in the country.  The Ministry of Tourism plays a crucial role in coordinating and supplementing the

APPROACH IN THE 10
th
 PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 2005-06
 
4.         The approach in the 10th Plan aims to stimulate investment and encourage the State Governments to develop unique tourism products. 
The State Governments would use Tourism as a means for achieving their socio-economic objectives and catalyze the private sector to enhance
investment in tourism.  It seeks to enhance the employment potential within the tourism sector as well as to foster economic integration through
developing linkages with other sectors.  The 10
th
 Plan acknowledges the traditionally recognised advantages of developing tourism for the

promotion of national integration, international understanding and the earning of foreign exchange besides recognising vast employment
generating potential of Tourism and furthering the socio-economic objectives of the Plan. It also seeks to provide legislative and regulatory
support for sustainable tourism and protect the interests of both the industry as well as the consumer. It further seeks to involve the rural sector
in the promotion of all rich areas of tourism viz., rural, heritage, adventure and eco-tourism.  It focuses on the development of competitive high
quality products and destinations besides addressing the concerns of growth through resolution of contradictions in policy so as to achieve
inter-sectoral convergence of activities that helps to foster the growth of tourism.

RURAL TOURISM
25.       Tourism growth potential can be harnessed as a strategy for rural development. The development of a strong platform around the
concept of Rural Tourism is definitely useful for a country like 
India
, where almost 74% of the population resides in its 7 million villages. 
Across the world, the trends of industrialisation and development have had an urban centric approach. Alongside, the stresses of urban
lifestyles have led to a "counter-
urbanization "
 syndrome. This has led to growing interest in the rural areas. At the same time, this trend of
urbanisation has led to falling income levels, lesser job opportunities in the rural areas leading to an urbanisation syndrome in the rural areas.
Rural Tourism is one of the few activities, which can provide a solution to these problems. Besides, there are other factors, which are shifting
the trend towards rural tourism like increasing levels of awareness, growing interest in heritage and culture and improved accessibility, and
environmental consciousness. In the developed countries, this has resulted in a new style of tourism of visiting village settings to experience
and live a relaxed and healthy lifestyle. This concept has taken the shape of a formal kind of Rural Tourism.  Ministry of Tourism gives
financial assistance to the State Governments for the Rural Tourism Projects.

HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
30.       Training programs in the field of Hotel Management, Catering and Nutrition were initiated by Government of India.  In order to harness
the resources and also to provide a central thrust to the program, Ministry of Tourism also established the National Council for Hotel
Management and Catering Technology (NCHMCT) in the year 1982.  The main objectives for setting up the Council at the apex level were:
 
(a)
          
To advise the Government on coordinated development of hotel management and catering education.
(b)
         
To collect, collate and implement international development in the area of human resource development for the hospitality sector.
(c)
          
To affiliate institutes and prescribe courses of study and instructions leading to examinations conducted by it.
(d)
         
To standardize courses and infrastructure requirements for institutes imparting education and training in hospitality management.
(e)
          
To prescribe educational and other qualifications, experience, etc. for members of staff in the affiliated institutes and organize faculty
development programs.
(f)
           
To award Certificates and Diplomas.
 
31.       As a result of vast expansion and modernization of the country
�
s hospitality industry, hotel management and catering education
programs gained tremendous popularity and the profile of students seeking admission to these courses also underwent a transformation.  The
courses offered by the National Council are of international standard which have been recognized by the hospitality industry.  At present, there
are 24 Institutes of Hotel Management and 6 Food Craft Institutes following National Council
�
s course curriculum.   National   Council   has
consistently worked on augmentation of training capacity in the different Institutes of Hotel Management.  As a result, there has been a
constant increase in the intake in the first year of the 3-Year Degree Program.  Compared to intake of 2760 in year 2003, the intake in year
2004 increased to 2915.

Rs.8.90 crore as against a loss of Rs.5.12 crore during the corresponding period last year.   The Committee hopes that careful planning for the
future would definitely help the ITDC in emerging as a self-sustained and profitable organization.

the country and promoting 
India
 as a 
tourists
 destination by providing all tourist services under a single umbrella.  The Committee takes note of
the fact that out of 26 hotel owned by ITDC, 18 hotels have been disinvested and activities of ITDC have been suitably restructured and

since ITDC is integral part of tourism sector its efficiency can be projected as a role model for the private sector.  The Committee therefore,

AT A GLANCE

           
APPROACH IN THE 10
th
 PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 2005-06
 
            
The Committee notes that the budgetary allocation has always been less than the actual requirement and to adjust the shortfall,
the allocation has to be subsequently increased.  The Committee is unable to comprehend the reasons for keeping lower outlays when
the actual requirement is far higher.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that every effort should be taken to make realistic
estimation of allocation in subsequent plans keeping in view all the anticipated demand for development of the tourism sector as a
whole.
(
Para
 9)
            The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism has been allocated a higher amount to the tune of Rs.786.00 crore in the B.E.
2005-06 which is almost 57 per cent over and above the approved outlay for the year 2004-05.  However, the Committee expresses its
concern over the under utilisations of funds by the Ministry during the year 2004-05 and notes that the Ministry could spend only 79
per cent of the allocation i.e. Rs.395.1 crore out of the budgeted allocation of Rs.500 crore upto February 2005.  The Committee also
notes that larger part of the budgeted amount was spent at the fag end of the financial year, especially, in the months of February and
March, which is much against the financial norms.  The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the programmes and policies
should be implemented in a manner which ensures regular infusion of funds in various projects/schemes uniformly in all quarters of
the financial year.  The Committee expects that the Ministry of Tourism will be in a better position to suitably revise the plan outlays
in future. 
(
Para
 13)
 
PRODUCT/ INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT OF DESTINATIONS AND CIRCUITS
 
            
The Committee notes that with an aim to improve the existing destinations and circuits and to develop new destinations and
tourists circuits of world class standard, the Ministry of Tourism has merged the existing two scheme of Integrated Development of
Tourist Circuit and Product/Infrastructure and destination development into one single scheme as Product/Infrastructure
Development of Destinations and Circuits.  However, the Committee is surprised to note that the tourism potential and uniqueness of
some of the important States like Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Tamilnadu, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and  Uttranchal for convergence of
resources and development of Circuits and Destinations of international importance has not yet been fully explored by the Ministry. 
The Committee recommends that more Circuits and Destinations  region-wise should be identified in consultation with the State
Governments and developed in an integrated and holistic manner for the purpose of convergence of resources and world-class
benchmarking, the related Ministries and Department of State Governments should have sub-plans in their annual plans so that
tourism related infrastructure projects receive the highest priority.
            The Committee also recommends that purposeful domestic and international publicity and marketing support should also be
provided to all important tourist Circuits and Destinations so as to create interest of the tourists in the Indian tourism products besides
promoting 
India
 as a major tourists destination.
            The Committee notes with serious concern that the Ministry of Tourism sanctioned 2526 numbers of small isolated projects
spread throughout the length and breadth of the country during 8
th
 and 9
th
 plan period, out of which, 708 projects remained still
incomplete.  The Committee feels that delay in implementation of projects not only led to slow progress and cost overrun but at the
same time, deprive the tourists of the desired facilities.  The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism will converge all the
resources required for development of 
tourists
 infrastructure instead of spreading it very thinly in small isolated projects.  The
Committee recommends that to meet the developmental objectives and convergence of resource, the State and Central Government
should work in synergetic manner and provide best facilities at the most economical price besides addressing the issues of civic
governance, management of sites and services, ensuring safety and security and hassle free comfortable stay for the tourists at these
projects sites.
 
            The Committee also recommends the Ministry to adopt a proactive approach and take care of the hindrances resulting in delay
and put in place some institutional mechanism to achieve better coordination, effective monitoring and timely implementation of these
pending projects.                     
(Paras 18,
  19
, 23 & 24)
RURAL TOURISM
            The Committee observes that Rural Tourism is an important way in addressing the impact of increasing trends of
industrialization and helps in moderating the stress of urban life styles and other syndromes and Ministry of Tourism is paying
adequate attention to the development of rural infrastructure in the country in participation with Private Sector with a view to
translate the structural changes into benefits at the grassroots level.  In this regard, the Committee reiterates its earlier
recommendation contained in 79
th
 Report on Demand for Grants 2004-05 of Ministry of Tourism which may be read as under:-
�
The Committee is of the view that Rural Tourism has great potential and prospects in the country as it helps to revive the
local peoples' interests and pride in their culture, tradition and values besides generating the tourists interest in the customs of
the indigenous people as it focuses directly on the local people.  The Committee feels that with a growing interest in the
intangible culture of different countries (i.e. lifestyle, cuisine, ceremonies, music, religion, beliefs, customs and history)
,
 there is
an enormous potential to encourage global tourism in rural areas. The Committee recommends the Ministry to develop some
institutional mechanism for supporting, promoting and organizing large number of fairs & festivals and handicrafts & craft
melas/bazaars in rural areas which will provide exposure, recognition as well as, additional flow of income to local artisans.  The
Committee further recommends that the Ministry should actively coordinate its efforts for liaising with other
Ministries/Departments of Government of India viz. Ministries of Rural Development, Environment and Forests, Textiles &
Culture etc. and other concerned organisation/agencies for converging of resource from that Ministry/Department and increase
allocation for tourism sector through the state budgets as tourism has a greater potential for creating a large-scale employment
opportunity than any other industry in the country

.
(Paras 29)
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
            
The Committee notes that there are 24 Institutes of Hotel Management and 6 Food Crafts Institutes catering to the
requirements of tourism and other industries for trained manpower.  The Committee is of the view that with the vast expansion and

modernisation of the hospitality sector, the Hotel Management and catering education programme gained tremendous popularity and
there is great demand for trained manpower not only in the field of hospitality sector but also it spanned to other sectors like Hospitals,
Call Centres, Banks etc.  The Committee observes that as number of hotels/restaurants
  are
 going to increase in the future, availability
of trained manpower is a must to meet the growing demand for excellence in the tourism sector.  The Committee recommends the
Ministry to set up Institutes of Hotel Management in each State for meeting shortage of trained manpower in the tourism and other
sectors.  The Committee further recommends that in view of the mushrooming of the number of such institutions mostly in the private
sector which does not have desired training level and infrastructure facilities, a statutory status to the National Council for Tourism &
Hospitality Education should be granted to better regulate and networking of all resources for institutions in the tourism and
hospitality sectors. 
(Paras 36)
PROVIDING A CONSTITUTIONAL STATUS TO TOURISM
            
The Committee notes that a proposal to include Tourism in the concurrent list has been mooted by the Ministry for giving
Constitutional recognition to tourism and development of tourism in a systematic manner.  As result of which so far as 29 States/Union
Territories have agreed for placing tourism in the concurrent list and 6 States have opposed the proposal.  The Committee feels that
India
�
s tourism products will grow only when the suitable legislative and regulatory support is provided.  The Committee, therefore,
recommends the Ministry of Tourism to build a strong national consensus for creating awareness about the role of tourism and
harness its benefits as an instrument of economic development and employment catalyst besides removing the hurdles for its growth
and every effort should be taken by the Ministry to include tourism in the Concurrent List of the Constitution.  
(Paras 39)
 
 
 
UNIFORMITY AND RATIONALISATION OF TAXES ON TRANSPORT AND HOSPITALITY SECTOR
 
            The Committee notes that the major barrier to the growth of tourism in the country is a multitude of Central and State level
taxes.  The Committee is of the opinion that uniform taxation is very necessary for promotion of tourism and recommends the
Ministry of Tourism to make consistent effort for building a nationwide campaign on rationalization of taxation issues both in
transport and hotel sectors.
(
Para
 43)
DOMESTIC TOURISM AND PUBLICITY
            
The Committee notes that during the year 2003, around 6 million Indians have visited abroad against a total incoming flow of
2.73 million foreign tourists,  and more and more countries are queuing up to attract the Indian tourists, which has led to foreign
exchange outflow.  The Committee observes that by diverting Indian tourists going abroad to Indian destinations, massive potential for
domestic tourism can be explored and this requires focussed approach for its growth.  The Committee is of the view that the growth of
global tourism depends upon the domestic tourism and it is easier to target the domestic tourism market as compared to the
international market.  The Committee feels that a relative change in the marketing strategy is required for tapping the domestic and
international tourism markets and recommends that special emphasis must be laid for accessing the market by consolidation of efforts
to arrest the increasing trend of outbound tourists.
            The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Ministry for launching a multi-pronged promotional campaign in all key markets
across the world under the brand name of 'Incredible 
India
'.  The Committee hopes that the campaign will continue to focus on the
diverse and varied tourism products of the country and will be able to create awareness about varied attractions amongst the
travelers.    The Committee notes that the outlay on publicity for 2005-06 has been increased to Rs.70 crore which is almost five times
as compared to that of last financial year.   The Committee hopes that with the increased outlay, the Ministry of Tourism will be able
to make effective publicity to promote domestic tourism.  However, the Committee recommends the Ministry to chalk-out a concrete
plan for targeting domestic middle class tourists. 
(Paras 48 & 49)
OVERSEAS PROMOTION AND MARKETING
            
The Committee is unhappy to note that there is a heavy shortfall in the utilization of funds for Overseas Promotion and
Marketing.  The Committee also notes that the Ministry has not given any reasons for under utilization of funds.  The Committee
observes that while revising allocation little consideration has been paid to the actual expenditure incurred in the past.  The Committee
hopes that the Ministry will be able to utilize the funds allocated during 2005-06 optimally.
The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism has reoriented itself to the overseas market with a view to changing global
resources and fierce competition in the tourism generating market and the allocation has substantially been increased during 2005-06. 
The Committee expects that number of Asian and particularly Chinese Tourists is expected to grow enormously as the Asia-Pacific
region becomes more integrated with the global economy and recommends the Ministry to develop linkages to tap tourists from these
countries especially Japan, Korea and China and create basic infrastructure to facilitate the global tourists arrivals from these
countries.
 
(Paras 53 & 54)
NATIONAL TOURISM PROMOTION BOARD
            
The Committee is unhappy to note the appalling state of co-ordination in the tourism sector.   The Committee feels that to
synergise the tourism potential in the country, coordination is needed as several Ministries are involved apart from State Governments,
other agencies and Private Sector.  The Committee desires the Ministry to create a framework, which facilitate and take everybody on
board.  The Committee recommends the Ministry to reconsider the matter to create National Tourism Promotion Board for
coordination with all these agencies in terms of policy decision and in the area of execution as recommended by the Committee in its
79
th
 Report on Demands for Grants (2004-05) of the Ministry of Tourism.

Regional Director should act as a bridge for close coordination in all tourism related issues besides holding periodical meetings of the
representatives of the State Tourism Departments, Tour & Travel operators  and other related organization for bringing out better
understanding and coordination.

SHORTAGE OF ACCOMODATION IN THE STAR AND BUDGET HOTELS
            
The Committee notes with serious concern that there is a shortfall in hotel accommodation in all star categories particularly in
the budget hotel segment though India is the second fastest growing country in the travel and Tourism sector and is growing at the rate
of 8.8% annually.  
India
 has witnessed a tremendous growth in tourism sector registering a positive growth of about 30.2% in domestic
tourism and increase of 23.5% in terms of foreign tourist arrivals. The Committee feels that poor tourism infrastructure may hinder
the growth of tourism.  The Committee observes that the accommodation shortage is due to scarcity of prime location and rigid land
use norms.  The Committee recommends the Ministry to take coordinated efforts with all the State/Union Territories for allotment of
plots at prime locations and provide incentives for meeting the demand.  Priority should also be given to meet increasing demand for
capacity addition and uplifting tourism infrastructure to support the growth of tourism in the country.
 
            The Committee is also of the view that Infrastructure is the key to the development of any economy and to boost economic
growth in the country. The Committee, therefore, recommends that a full-fledged infrastructure status should be given to tourism and
hospitality sector for the growth of tourism in a big way.

            The Committee is constrained to note that the Ministry of Tourism could utilize only Rs.6.55 crore for Computerisation and

priority the Ministry of Tourism attached to the Computerisation and Information Technology Development.     The Committee feels
that the Ministry of Tourism is giving little attention to the Information Technology initiatives and has not achieved much progress in
this field, which is very crucial for providing vital information to the tourist at the shortest time span.  However, the Committee notes
that the Ministry of Tourism is planning to introduce a toll free Telecom based facilitation service for the benefit of tourists and the
existing official website on tourism has also been revamped to provide reliable and detailed information on 
India
 and Indian tourism
products.  The Committee hopes that this facility will be made available to the tourists within the stipulated period of six months. The
Committee feels that the concentration has to be focused on certain areas especially at grass root level and recommends that there
should be a centralized system for dissemination of all essential information through the web database so as to establish a vital linkage
with the people at large and the website should also be linked with all the State websites.  The Committee notes that the present official
website on tourism has a lot of information but these are essentially static data.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that the
website must provide for interactive space from anywhere in the world as per its earlier recommendation contained in 79
th
 Report on
Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Tourism.

The Committee is of the view that Andaman & Nicobar Islands with its flora, fauna, forest and underwater marine life, have
the potential of growing into top tourist destinations in the world.  However, the tourism scenario in the island has been severely
affected by tsunami recently and there is an urgent need to rebuild the image of the islands and gain the confidence of the tourists.  The
Committee recommends that Government of India should, in coordination with the local Government formulate specific programme

for capital investment and rebuilding the infrastructure by giving subsidy and incentives, in a time bound manner besides opening of
more Islands for the Indian as well as foreign tourists to generate employment opportunities and strengthening the overall economy of
the Islands keeping in view the ecological and anthropological sustainability of the region.
            The Committee further recommends that the Government should provide concessions/incentives as applicable to the Industrial
sector 
viz.
 water, electricity, municipality tax, interest of loans, etc. to all those engaged in tourism promotional activities in the Union
Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands as per the Orders of the Administration No.1055 dated 6
th
 March, 1986.

tourists
 inflow.  The Committee recommends that LTC facility to Andaman and 
Nicobar
Islands
 should be introduced from Kolkata also, to encourage the inflow of domestic tourists to these islands.  Further direct flights
should be introduced to Port Blair from other stations in the country apart from Kolkata and Chennai.  Private airlines should also be

Islands
.  In order to optimally exploit the tourism potential of these islands, the Committee recommends that
the tourists should be granted long term visa and restricted area permit so that they could spend more and more time at these 
Islands
. 
            The Committee also recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should supplement the efforts of the Andaman and Nicobar
Administration for advertising and promoting Andaman Tourism through electronic, print and display and exhibition media. 
            The Committee notes that Andaman and 
Nicobar Islands
 consist of 512 
Green
 
Islands
.  The Committee observes that one of the
major impediments in the growth of the tourism in the Island is the way in which the Metrological Department and the media spread

Islands
 of Andaman and Nicobar 
Islands
.  On many occasions, the
Central areas of Andaman and 
Nicobar 
Islands
 are unaffected by these earthquakes.  However, the impression gathered from the news
flashed is that all the islands including those major tourist centers of Andaman and

 have been rocked by these

deter
 the flow of tourist to visit these

.  The

DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM IN NORTH-EASTERN REGION
The Committee expresses its serious concern on the indiscriminate mining activities and desires the Ministry of Tourism to
develop these caves as a unique tourism product.
            The Committee is constrained to note that some of the major impediments for the growth and development of tourism in North
Eastern Region are weak road links, inadequate Rail and Air connectivity, high luxury tax on room rents, high inter-state permit tax,
lack of parking facilities, frequent check-posts on National Highways, mandatory permit system, ILP/RAP/PAP, law and order
situation, bottlenecks in infrastructure amenities, financial constraints, trained man-power, monitoring and coordination and lack of
entrepreneurship etc.  The Committee emphasizes upon the need for comprehensive and integrated approach to resolve the problems
faced by the North East region and to take measures for infrastructure and destination development besides prioritizing the projects to
give renewed boost to the development of tourism in the region. 
            The Committee feels that tourism cannot grow optimally without private sector participation and stresses upon the need to
attract Private Sector investment for development of tourism in the region and private entrepreneurs should be given some
incentives/concessions besides efforts should be made to declare tourism as an Industry so that the States would benefit from Central
incentives. 
            The Committee is unhappy to know about the lack of proper coordination between the Ministry of Tourism, North East
Development Council, and Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region and desires that to in order to harness the National
Development priorities and to boost tourism industry as a whole in the North East region, proper coordination must be established and
North East Development Council should be strengthened with more powers so that it could take a leading role for the overall
development of the region from its present role of mere an advisory body.
            The Committee notes with concern the inconveniences faced by the tour operators and tourism due to the mandatory need to
obtain Inner Line Permit while passing through the State of Nagaland and imposition of RAP/PAP in all North-East States except
Assam.  Due to disturbed area tag put on these states, besides restrictions on foreign tourists to stay beyond permitted period in these
States except Assam has discouraged the foreign tourist arrivals in Noeth-East Region.  The Committee recommends that in order to
optimally exploit the potential of tourism in these States, the restriction on foreign tourists visiting the States and permit system should
be scraped at once and they may be permitted to stay for longer periods to enjoy the natural beauty of the States.  The Committee also
recommends the Ministry of Tourism to take up the matter for scraping of Permit System for North Eastern States with the Ministry
of Home Affairs.

2.         At the outset, the Chairman of the Committee extended a warm welcome to the representatives of the Ministry of Tourism, Government
of India, State Tourism Department and the Tour/Travel and Hoteliers' Associations.
 
3.         In order to have a proper assessment of the problems faced by tourism industry, the Committee initially heard the representatives of the
travel/tour and hoteliers' associations.  The representatives of the JAC Tourist Inter State Bus Services informed the Committee that Inter State
Bus Service is a major means of communication between Manipur and other States.  However NH-39 and NH-53 connecting Imphal to
Guwahati 
via
 Dimapur and Imphal to Silchar 
via
 Jine were in bad shape.  As a result the journey become tiring, time consuming and
discouraged the tourists from coming to the State.  It was also pointed out that frequent check posts on the 
National 
Highway
 in the
neighboring state of Nagaland has also caused a lot of hardship to the tour operators, the drivers and the passengers.   He also highlighted the
need for reduction in the overall Inter State Permit Tax and present high fees at the time of obtaining countersignature on a reciprocal basis and

in line with the tax and fees levied in other States.  Also there was lack of parking facility for the 
Inter
 
State
 buses operating in NH-39 which
resulted in inconvenience to the tourists as well as the transport agencies.
 
4.         One of the representatives of the travel industry gave a brief insight on the tourism potentials of the state like the well-known Loktak
Lake, Shiroi Peak, Sangai, the only deer found in the floating park at Keibul Lamjao or the floating island etc. which were yet to be exploited
to the fullest.  He also dwelt on the many inconveniences faced by the tour operators and tourists due to the mandatory need to obtain Inner
Line Permit while passing through the state of Nagaland and imposition of RAP/PAP in the state due to the disturbed area tag which has dealt a
significant blow to the inflow of tourists.  He also proposed for additional flights as the present arrangements do not meet the demand of the
people particularly during imposition of Bandhs and strikes, which have become a regular feature in the State. It was brought out that although
it had been declared that tourists can enter Manipur by road from Kohima side through NH-39, but in actual practice they were not being
granted permits.  These representatives also pointed out that Imphal is not connected with train which compels the use of air services, which are
quite expensive.  The representatives also complained about the lack of adequate number of flights operating to Manipur and requested for
additional flights to Manipur.
 
5.         The Committee then interacted with the representatives of Ministry of Tourism, Government of India and the State Government.  The
representatives of State Government made a brief power-point presentation on Manipur Tourism.  They also highlighted the limitations in the
development of tourism attributing it to the law and order situation, bottlenecks in infrastructure amenities, weak road link, weak
entrepreneurship, financial constraint of the State etc.  While talking of the measures for giving renewed boost to development of tourism, they
suggested reduction in luxury tax etc. on room rent, entertainment, enactment and adoption of tourism policy, lifting of Inner Line Permit,
RAP/PAP, increase in flight frequency, Regular bus service between 
Myanmar
 (Mondalay) and Manipur (Imphal), extension of rail link to
Noney etc.
 
6.         The Committee noted that from the 7
th
 Plan onwards upto early 2001, the Government of India had sanctioned 63 projects in the State
and also released considerable amount of money.  However, the State Government had been able to complete only 10 projects.  The Committee
enquired about the poor performance of the State Government in the execution of the tourism projects.  In response, the Committee was
apprised by the representatives of State Government that there were various reasons for non-completion of projects, such as non-availability of
land, wrong selection of sites, law and order situation and non-release of money deposited in the Government Account by the Finance
Department.  As a result, tourism scenario in Manipur had taken a back seat.
 
7.         The Committee enquired about the steps taken by the State Government to change the scenario and for development of tourism in the
State.  In response, it was informed that the Government had taken a hardened step to review and revamp the existing schemes based on the
actual ground situation, by completing those that are nearing completion, by dropping those that have not been started or found unfeasible and
non-viable and replacing them with fresh viable schemes.  The decision of the State Government has also been intimated to the Government of
India.  The representatives of the State Government also expressed the hope that with the revamping and reviewing of the existing schemes,
there will be no dearth of tourists to the State in the near future.
 
8.         The Committee appreciated the change being made but stated that the reviewing of the schemes alone will not serve the purpose
because some self effort and accountability has to be there for the financial loss and some corrective measures need to be taken to bring back a
system that had gone bad.
 
9.         The Committee then enquired from the representatives of Ministry of Tourism, Government of India about the non-completion etc. of
the centrally sponsored schemes by the State.  The Committee was of the view that the Government of India could not be absolved of its
responsibility of assessment about the viability of the projects sponsored by the State Government. The representatives of the Ministry of
Tourism informed the Committee that the present procedure was that the State Government prepares the feasibility report/project subject to
availability of land, fund of the project which is the sole responsibility of the State Government and that further fund is released as per the
Utilisation Certificate submitted by the State Government.  In response to another query, the Committee was informed that North-East Council
(NEC) and the Ministry of Tourism were working together with a positive approach to bring tourism to the forefront in Manipur.
 
10.       The Committee then advised that the Regional Director (NE) of Ministry of Tourism should hold periodical meeting of the
representatives of State Tourism Department, tour/travel operators and other related organizations for bringing out better understanding and
coordination.  The Committee also emphasized that to attract private sector investment for development of tourism in the State, the private
entrepreneurs, in return, need to be offered some incentives/concessions etc.
           
11.       The meeting ended at

2.         At the outset, the Chairman of the Committee extended warm welcome to the representatives of the Ministry of Tourism, Government
of India, State Tourism Department and the Tour/Travel and Hoteliers' Association.  The representatives of the State Tourism Department also
welcomed the Chairman and the Members of the Committee and thanked them for having visited Mizoram to assess the development of
tourism in the State.
 
3.         The Committee initially heard the representatives of the travel/tour and hoteliers' associations to become aware of the problems faced
by them.  The points raised by these representatives are as under:-
 
(i)
                  
The Hotel Industry is not accepted as an Industry in Mizoram despite the fact that it had been published in the Mizoram gazette
that Hotels are under the Industry Department.
(ii)
                
The Hotel license is issued by the Local Administration Department but no 
support have
 been given by any Department of the
State and Central Government for promotion of the Hotels in Mizoram.
(iii)       The requirement of capital investment in hotel industry is much higher compared to other States due to the transportation cost
but the tariff is much lower than the neighbouring States.  It was pointed out that although the occupancy rate in the hotels was
60% yet the hotels were not making profits since they were providing a lot of facilities at limited rates.
(iv)       The
 electricity bill and water transportation cost are very costly and as such       the maintenance cost was very high.
(v)        Inadequate mobile telephone service - due to the topography and insufficient transmitter towers, not all areas are reachable even
within the town and a lot depends on which side of the hill you are.  Also there is no prepaid card facility for mobile service. 
 
4.         The representatives pointed out that in view of the aforesaid factors, the cost of management of hotels was very high and the people of
Mizoram were running after shopping complexes instead of hotel industry.  These representatives requested for a strong support from the State
Government as well as the Central Government to promote the hotel industry in Mizoram.
 
5.         The representatives of travel agency pointed out that foreign tourists were permitted to stay for only 10 days, which was a very short
period.  They requested that the foreign tourists should be permitted to stay for at least 25 days.  Further, the Protected Area Permitted (PAP)
was valid within Aizawl city only and most of the good tourist spots were at the outskirts of the city.  They requested that the PAP holders
should be allowed to visit any tourist spot within the permitted time.  The Committee pointed out that the above issues were within the purview
of Ministry of Home Affairs and promised to take up the issue with the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
6.         The Committee then interacted with the representatives of Central Ministry of Tourism and the State Government. The representatives
of State Government made a brief power-point representation on the prospects of tourism in Mizoram.  The Committee was informed that
Mizoram was under insurgency for two decades.  Due to long period of insurgency Mizoram is still lagging behind other States in development
activities in general and in development of tourism infrastructure in particular.  There is shortage of tourist accommodation even in the capital
city of 
Aizawl
.  Participation from the private sector is almost absent in hotel and restaurant business.  The immediate need for promotion of
tourism in the State is development of more tourist accommodations in Aizawl and other important places and also development of other
facilities along the highways. 
 
7.         The Committee was also apprised that road connectivity was lacking to various places where eco-tourism and adventure tourism could
be developed.  Basic infrastructure like power and water supply were also lacking.  The only National Highway NH-54 was also in a bad
condition.  Further, there were frequent delays and cancellation of the flights operating to the state.
 
8.         The Committee advised the State Government that they should work towards publicizing and promoting North-east as a whole instead
of projecting only Mizoram as a tourist destination.  This could go a long way in forceful presentation of their views to the Central and State
Governments for the development of tourism in the North-eastern region of the country. 
 
9.         The meeting ended at 
6.30 p.m.
 with a vote of thanks to the Chair.
